stories.t: On the Road in Atlanta: Messy Data, Runaway Pilots, and Lessons from the GDS AI Summit
stories.s: Greg Lambert and Marlene Gebauer record a podcast from Atlanta after the GDS AI Summit, discussing messy data, unclear data ownership and pressures on legal technology. It is commentary rather than news.
stories.o: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

stories.t: How Legal Teams Can Withstand Scrutiny Across Investigations, Privacy, and AI: eDiscovery Webinars
Stephenson Harwood lines up new chief exec amid Taylor Wessing merger talks
‘He’s stuck his neck out’ – national law firm leaders size up Burnham’s devolution drive
stories.s: Legal Business gathers reactions from national law firm leaders to Andy Burnham's devolution drive, including a quote from Sarah Walton, managing partner at Weightmans, who says the Manchester buzz around Number 10 North will fade and outcomes will matter. The piece focuses on the political agenda for the North of England.

stories.t: Judiciary gives AI cautious thumbs-up (but draws line at robot judges)
stories.s: The judiciary has given a cautious endorsement to the use of AI, promoting strict safeguards and robust testing, but has drawn a line at robot judges, according to Legal Cheek. The extract is brief and does not name the judicial body or the guidance.

stories.t: SRA names new chair - with pledge to lead change
stories.s: Caroline Corby is to become chair of the Solicitors Regulation Authority, replacing Anna Bradley, according to The Law Society Gazette. Corby joins from a healthcare regulator. The report says she has pledged to lead change.

stories.t: 'Dark day for international justice': legal chiefs condemn US sanctions on ICC
stories.s: The Law Society and the International Bar Association condemned US sanctions on the International Criminal Court, saying perpetrators of serious crimes may escape punishment. A landmark report also found weaknesses in the UK approach to atrocity crimes.

stories.t: High Court chastises MoD over repeated deadline failures
Law Society highlights plight of 'vital' small firms
stories.s: The Law Society says small firms are vital and that their sustainability is likely to be a key focus at the Society's AGM. The item is a brief preview from the Law Society Gazette.

stories.t: Barrister who was part of £1.8m legal aid scam disbarred
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that a barrister involved in a £1.8m legal aid fraud has been disbarred. The practitioner was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court in June 2024 to three years' imprisonment. The report concerns professional regulation and sanctions for a member of the bar convicted over the scheme.

stories.t: ‘Bankruptcy Tourism’ Ruling Prompts New Ch. 15 Challenges
stories.s: Troutman Pepper Locke partner Evelyn J. Meltzer was quoted on 13 October 2026 on a bankruptcy tourism ruling and new Chapter 15 challenges. The firm published the commentary on its own site.

stories.t: A ‘Spirit of Amity’ and the Original Meaning of Civility: Derek Webb’s thoughts at ABA Annual
Trump Propaganda Ads Outlast Court Order Thanks To One Unopened Email — See Also
stories.s: Above the Law reports that the DOJ attributed its breach of a judge's order on Trump propaganda ads to an unread email. The roundup also mentions Quinn Emanuel's work from anywhere policy and a comment on James Ho. The extract is a short news digest.

stories.t: This Biglaw Co-Founder’s Side Project Was Engineering A Revolution
James Ho Demands First Amendment Right To Post Covert Bathroom Pics
Goodwin Partner Launches US AI-Native Law Firm Arm
Harvey Launches Intake for Inhouse Teams
stories.s: Harvey has launched Intake, a new legal front door for in-house teams, according to Artificial Lawyer. The tool funnels contracts to the right lawyers, and the extract indicates it does more than that. Details are limited in the extract.

stories.t: From AI Tools to Agentic AI – A Roadmap
stories.s: Paul Walker, Global Solutions Director at iManage, has written an Artificial Lawyer opinion piece setting out a roadmap from AI tools to agentic AI. He argues that law firms have long delegated work to less experienced staff. The extract is an opinion piece by a vendor executive.

stories.t: How Does the Online Bail Bond Application Process Work in Florida?
When Should a Business Seek Legal Guidance on Privacy and Cybersecurity?
What Employment Issues Can Affect Executives and Senior Employees?
Latham’s London Partner Yen Sum Named to 100 Most Influential Women in European Finance List 2026
Head of CPS and health regulator named new SRA chair
Law Society puts recruitment at heart of small firm manifesto
stories.s: The Law Society has set out a small firm manifesto that puts recruitment at its centre, according to Legal Futures. It calls for funding for solicitor apprenticeships at SME law firms to be available regardless of age, to address recruitment problems.

stories.t: Drivers “eye litigation” with FCA motor finance case set for February
stories.s: Legal Futures reports that drivers are considering litigation rather than waiting for the legal challenge to the FCA motor finance compensation scheme. The challenge's hearing has now been set for February. The extract is brief and does not give the hearing's court or further detail.

stories.t: Avoidable requisitions plummet amid warning of ethical dimension
stories.s: Legal Futures reports that HM Land Registry says applications with avoidable requisitions have fallen and are now almost half their 2022 level, with a warning on the ethical dimension.

stories.t: Law firms and in-house teams face “AI governance gap”
Four firms land roles on year’s biggest UK pension risk transfer
Investment in legal tech set for record -breaking year as market shows sign of maturity
New Flood Performance Certificates piloted alongside resources platform
Latest quarterly conveyancing sentiment survey launched
stories.s: The Council for Licensed Conveyancers has launched its latest quarterly conveyancing sentiment survey, the Quarterly Confidence Tracker. Views on this month's budget are expected to dominate.

stories.t: AI, reform and planning: What’s on the agenda for the 2026 SLC annual conference
stories.s: The Society of Licensed Conveyancers has released the agenda for its 2026 annual conference and dinner. Topics include conveyancing reform and AI, along with planning, according to Today's Conveyancer. The extract lists speakers from conveyancing, legal and property sectors.

stories.t: The Conveyancing Improvement Collective (CIC) – Coming to a town near you
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer publishes a column by Rob Hailstone on why buying and selling a home takes so long. He points to rising transaction times and high fall-through rates, and argues that meaningful change needs greater industry collaboration. The piece is opinion rather than reported news.

stories.t: Extension of temporary Litigation Practice Rights Portfolio evidence adjustments
stories.s: CILEx Regulation has extended temporary evidence adjustments for the Litigation Practice Rights Portfolio. The extract gives no detail of the adjustments or the new end date.

stories.t: Pay for AI by Reshuffling the Budget, Then Ask Permission to Reshuffle
stories.s: Axiom, a vendor, argues that in-house teams must reshuffle existing budgets to pay for AI, citing its 2027 In-House Legal Budget Report. The report says most AI initiatives get no dedicated budget.

stories.t: The Part of Background Screening Compliance That Falls on You – AssureHire
stories.s: Mitratech's AssureHire blog says employers face adverse action disputes and FCRA scrutiny over background screening compliance. It argues obligations extend beyond delivery of the report.

stories.t: See How Enterprise Legal Teams Are Building Defensible Hold Programs
stories.s: Mitratech promotes an on-demand webinar on how enterprise legal teams build defensible legal hold programmes. The post is a vendor event notice with no further detail in the extract.

stories.t: The CCBE at the Internation Bar Association’s Annual Conference – CCBE
stories.s: The CCBE, the body representing Europe's bar associations, has published an item on its participation at the International Bar Association's Annual Conference. No further text is available in the extract, so the topics discussed and any outcomes cannot be confirmed. The item concerns bar representation rather than a specific legal technology product.

stories.t: Treasury's First Outbound Investment Penalty: Implications for Private Fund Sponsors and Cross-Border Investment Activity
Colorado’s New Rules for Robots: Proposed Rules Cover ADMT and AI Chatbots | Morrison Foerster
stories.s: Morrison Foerster reviews Colorado's proposed rules on automated decision-making technology and AI chatbots. The extract is only the firm's boilerplate, so the detail of the rules is not available.

stories.t: The National Fraud Enforcement Division Announces Comprehensive Fraud Enforcement Methodology
stories.s: Willkie Farr & Gallagher has published a note on the National Fraud Enforcement Division's comprehensive fraud enforcement methodology. The source gives no date or further detail in the extract.

stories.t: DOJ Puts Sue Mi Terry Foreign-Agent Case on Hold
Kirkland leads for data centre recruitment as lateral hiring at US firms hits new peak
stories.s: Legal Business reports new research on law firms active in the data centre sector. Kirkland and Ellis, Greenberg Traurig and Dentons are named among the most active recruiters, and 191 partners with data centre expertise are cited. The research says lateral hiring across US firms has reached a new peak.

stories.t: Awkward! Legal AI rivals Legora and Harvey unveil same-named products just hours apart
stories.s: Legal Cheek reports that legal AI rivals Legora and Harvey each unveiled a product named Intake within hours of one another. The extract is brief, so the details of the two launches are not set out here. The coincidence of identical product names is the story's main point, and it matters to legal AI buyers and to the two vendors' marketing teams.

stories.t: Claimants' champion Day to step down - but not out
Revamped Courts and Tribunals Bill passes crucial hurdle
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that the revamped Courts and Tribunals Bill has passed a key stage and now sits with the House of Lords. The bill is designed to cut the Crown court backlog, according to the extract. The report gives no date for the Lords stages or the vote count.

stories.t: Could artificial intelligence destroy us all?
Quinn Emanuel adds new caveats to its ‘work from anywhere’ policy
Stress, drinking, gambling among problems lawyers report in new mental health study
stories.s: A new mental health study of lawyers, based on an Illinois survey, finds more than half report stress, excessive workloads and feeling unappreciated. Problem drinking and gambling are also reported among the issues.

stories.t: Democratic Midterm Gains Could Speed US Military Aid To Ukraine, Lawmaker Says
Manitoba bill to remove intimate partner violence time bar
Say what: non-disparagement clauses and the cost of breach
stories.s: Canadian Lawyer explains how non-disparagement clauses in settlements work, covering breach, scope and enforceability under Canadian courts. The piece is a publication feature with no named case or figure given in the extract.

stories.t: Stephenson Harwood names new leader as Taylor Wessing merger talks continue
Form: Apply to file a statement or declaration out of time, or an extension of time for traffic enforcement charges: Form TE14
stories.s: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has published form TE14, which lets people apply to file a statement or declaration out of time, or for an extension, in traffic enforcement cases. The form refers to statements (TE13) and declarations (PE3). It is an official procedural document for applicants in England and Wales.

stories.t: Form: Apply to challenge a traffic enforcement order: Form TE13
stories.s: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has published form TE13, which allows people to challenge a traffic enforcement order. The form covers moving traffic offences outside London only, and parking offences inside or outside London. It is an official procedural document for applicants.

stories.t: When time is money: A smarter AI stack for personal injury firms
Regulatory Change Automation: Infrastructure, Not a Tool for Legal Ops
stories.s: Neota Logic, a legal technology vendor, promotes its approach to regulatory change automation, turning regulatory changes into assigned, auditable actions for legal operations teams. The piece is vendor marketing without a stated date or figure.

stories.t: Legal AI rivals Harvey and Legora are seeing double
stories.s: Nonbillable reports that Harvey and Legora have each unveiled a product called Intake, just hours apart. The item is short and gives no further detail on the features or pricing of either product. It covers the same episode as the Legal Cheek report on the two launches.
